{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Consulting Services Agreement (Clear Capital as Customer)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review findings — 19 rules assessed, all findings verified

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed the playbook review of the Agreement. The commercial architecture is favourable to us: engagement is task-by-task under Statements of Work, there is no exclusivity, no minimum commitment, no most-favoured-nation obligation, no auto-renewal, no liquidated damages or exit fee, no non-compete on us, and no Vendor audit right against us. Most importantly, ownership of the Works vests in Clear Capital on payment, with only a narrow retained-tools carve-out and a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence back to us — this meets the fallback and most of the preferred position, so we are not redlining Section 4's ownership construct.

Ten items require attention. One is walk-away territory: the Agreement contains **no indemnity in either direction** — Section 7 is captioned "Indemnification of Contractor" but delivers only a liability cap and damages waivers, so we have no IP defence despite receiving software deliverables. Alongside that, there is **no conformance warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy** (implied warranties are disclaimed), **no exit provisions at all** (no transition assistance, no data return, no certified deletion), **no convenience exit while a Statement of Work is live**, and a liability cap of undefined duration with no carve-outs. The licence to us does not reach affiliates and cannot travel to an M&A successor; assignment is consent-gated with no successor carve-out. Governing law is Arizona with mandatory arbitration, both outside our accepted list. Insurance is close — E&O and CGL floors are met — but there is no cyber or privacy cover despite Contractor personnel accessing our facilities and systems.

Our proposed redlines are targeted at the fallback positions, not the preferred positions, and we have deliberately left untouched the provisions that already run in our favour (including the gating condition in Section 6 that prevents Contractor walking away mid-engagement).

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section (per finding) | Position / proposed action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | Works are Company property on payment; retained-tools carve-out with perpetual royalty-free sublicensable licence back. Minor wording gaps (no express "irrevocable"/"worldwide", no affirmative data-retention sentence) noted, not redlined. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Consent is mutual and "not unreasonably withheld", but there is no M&A or affiliate carve-out. Add mutual successor-assignment carve-out on written notice; no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists, so no walk-away trigger. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | "Company" is Clear Capital alone, so the § 4(c) licence excludes affiliates, and the consent-gated assignment clause blocks transfer to a successor. Extend the licence to affiliates on written notice and make it transferable to an M&A successor. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 6 Termination | Convenience right exists only when no Statement of Work is outstanding, i.e. only when no work is running; no refund of prepaid fees. Add a Company-only right to terminate on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund, leaving the mutual 15-day right and the Vendor-side restraint intact. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | Task-by-task engagement; no requirements, volume, sole/preferred-provider or third-party sourcing restriction. Preferred position. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 6 Termination | Time-and-materials only; 15 days' notice with no exit payment; on termination Contractor recovers only fees earned through the effective date. Preferred position. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | No restrictive covenant on us; § 4(b)(ii) is a licence-scope limit on Contractor's own pre-existing materials, not a business restraint. Preferred position. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Arizona law plus mandatory binding arbitration; both fallback elements fail. Substitute New York law and exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with the heading renamed so no arbitration reference dangles. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Mutual and limited to personnel directly involved (two fallback elements met), but runs term-plus-one-year and has no carve-outs. Re-anchor to 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement and add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 6 Termination | No transition assistance, data return/export or deletion obligation anywhere. Insert one paragraph: six months' assistance at then-current rates (90 days as fallback), 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion after return. Generic "Company data" wording used as "Customer Data" is undefined. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5 Contractor's Representations and Warranties and Warranty Disclaimer | No conformance warranty, no warranty period, no remedy; implied warranties disclaimed. Insert fallback: 90 days for software deliverables, 30 days for Services, with repair, replacement or refund. Existing disclaimer preserves express warranties and needs no amendment. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No Vendor audit, inspection or records-examination right; better than the preferred checklist. Do not volunteer audit machinery. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No MFN, best-pricing or right-to-match obligation on us. Preferred position. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume commitments | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall, guaranteed-hours or usage cap; we pay only for Services ordered and performed. Preferred position. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | Single continuing term until terminated; no automatic renewal, so no notice window or uplift mechanic. Contractor's uncapped 30-day rate-change right is noted for the file under pricing, not flagged here. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | No operative indemnity in either direction; § 5(c) gives a non-infringement warranty with no defence or remedy, and the § 7(a) cap would limit recovery. Insert Contractor IP indemnity for the Services and Works with customary modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace and refund remedies, and a 3x annual fees super-cap overriding § 7(a). **Walk-away item.** |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Workers' comp, USD 1m CGL per occurrence, USD 1m professional E&O and certificates on request meet the E&O floor, but there is no cyber or privacy cover despite personnel accessing our facilities and systems. Add USD 2m cyber/privacy liability; higher preferred limits noted as a further ask only. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Mutual cap and mutual consequential waiver are in place, but the cap basis has no duration and the sole exception is a dangling cross-reference to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor). Set both caps at fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim and add one mutual carve-out sentence for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. |

**Drafting note:** the operative paragraph numbers cited in several findings (non-assignability at Paragraph 10, governing law at Paragraph 11, non-solicitation at Paragraph 13, insurance at Paragraph 14, arbitration at Paragraph 19) do not align with the section headings against which those findings are anchored, and § 6(c) appears misplaced within § 7. We should tidy the cross-references and clause numbering in the same turn as the substantive edits.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **No Vendor IP indemnity (INDEMN, § 7).** The Agreement contains no indemnity, hold-harmless or defence obligation in either direction, while we take delivery of software Works. The § 5(c) non-infringement warranty carries no defence or remedy and any recovery would be squeezed by the § 7(a) cap. Per the playbook, the total absence of a Vendor IP indemnity is walk-away territory. We must land at least the fallback indemnity with the 3x annual fees super-cap; we should not sign without it.

No other finding reaches walk-away. In particular, there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right (ASSIGN), and the Section 6 gating condition prevents Contractor abandoning a live Statement of Work (T4C).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the ten open items, each drafted to the fallback and no further: IP indemnity with super-cap; conformance warranty (90/30 days, repair-replace-refund); transition assistance, data return and certified deletion in the Termination section; Company-only convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; licence extension to affiliates and M&A successors; successor-assignment carve-out; New York law and New York County courts in place of arbitration; 12-month non-solicit re-anchoring with carve-outs; 12-month liability cap with mutual carve-outs; USD 2m cyber/privacy insurance.
2. **Prioritise for negotiation** in this order: IP indemnity (walk-away), warranty and remedies, exit/transition and data return, convenience termination, then liability cap carve-outs. Licence portability, assignment, governing law, non-solicit and insurance are lower-friction and should be presented as a package.
3. **Hold the line on the favourable terms** — ownership under § 4, no exclusivity, no minimums, no MFN, no auto-renewal, no liquidated damages and no Vendor audit right. We should not volunteer audit machinery or trade any of these to buy the indemnity; if Contractor later requests verification rights, cap them at the fallback (once per year, 15 days' notice, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%).
4. **Flag to the business** Contractor's uncapped right to change rates on 30 days' notice (§ 3). This is a pricing point rather than a renewal-uplift deviation, but commercial should decide whether to seek a cap before signature.
5. **Cross-reference clean-up** of the paragraph numbering, the misplaced § 6(c) and the dangling "Paragraph 9" exception, to be handled alongside the substantive edits.
6. **Note on residual preferred asks** we have not pursued in this pass, available if the negotiation opens up: express "irrevocable/worldwide" licence wording and an affirmative data-retention statement; higher insurance limits (USD 2m CGL aggregate, USD 2m E&O, USD 5m cyber); a USD 1,000,000 liability floor with data protection, fraud and IP carve-outs and a payment-obligations exclusion; and six-month (rather than 90-day) transition assistance."}
